#!/bin/sh
# full_test.sh — scoring entry point. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.
#
# `drydock uat` runs `sh sources/full_test.sh` from the completed application root and takes its
# exit code and output as the score.

# "the application provides a POSIX-compatible bin/test.sh" a product requirement (st-001), so the
# tests are part of the deliverable. This harness is therefore a dispatcher, and its whole value
# is that it is still Commander-owned. An absent bin/test.sh is a delivered product that failed to
# meet st-001, which this script reports as a failure — rather than leaving the release gate with
# no oracle at all, where an unbuilt project grades PASSED by default.
set -eu

    echo "error: no bin/test.sh at the application root." >&2
    echo "st-001 requires the application to provide a POSIX-compatible bin/test.sh that exits" >&2
    echo "zero when every automated test passes." >&2

Shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here.

SQLite is the development and test engine. It parses the same declaration PostgreSQL does and
ignores what it does not enforce — ``VARCHAR(n)`` length in particular — so one rendered schema
serves both engines and nothing is stripped for one of them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
import threading
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

try:
    from .db import Driver
except ImportError:  # flat layout
    from db import Driver

__all__ = ["SqliteDriver"]


class SqliteDriver(Driver):
    """One connection per thread, opened on first use in that thread.

    A ``sqlite3.Connection`` belongs to the thread that created it and raises ``ProgrammingError``
    when used from another, so a single connection opened during construction is valid in no web
    request at all. This is not concurrency: queries stay sequential within a workflow, and the
    rule only stops one connection being shared across unrelated ones.
    """

    paramstyle = "qmark"
    returning = False

    def __init__(self, dsn: str) -> None:
        self._path = _path_from(dsn)
        self._local = threading.local()

    def connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        connection = getattr(self._local, "connection", None)
        if connection is None:
            if self._path != ":memory:":
                Path(self._path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # Autocommit by default; an explicit BEGIN suspends it until ROLLBACK.
            connection = sqlite3.connect(self._path, isolation_level=None)
            connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
            connection.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
            self._local.connection = connection
        return connection

    def close(self) -> None:
        connection = getattr(self._local, "connection", None)
        if connection is not None:
            connection.close()
            self._local.connection = None

    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:
        return cursor.lastrowid


def _path_from(dsn: str) -> str:
    """Read a filesystem path out of a DSN, accepting a bare path as well as a URL."""
    if "://" not in dsn:
        return dsn or ":memory:"
    _, _, remainder = dsn.partition("://")
    return remainder or ":memory:"

"""Shared pytest configuration for the ReadingList test suite.

Fixtures for the web client and database session are added by the application
and persistence stories; this foundation only fixes the project root on the path.
"""

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def project_root() -> Path:
    """Return the application root directory."""
    return PROJECT_ROOT
"""Foundation checks: project tree, dependency manifest, and pytest runner."""

import importlib.metadata
import sys
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path


def _load_pyproject(project_root: Path) -> dict:
    with open(project_root / "pyproject.toml", "rb") as handle:
        return tomllib.load(handle)


def test_declares_supported_python_version(project_root: Path) -> None:
    data = _load_pyproject(project_root)

    assert data["project"]["requires-python"] == ">=3.11"


def test_runtime_dependencies_include_flask(project_root: Path) -> None:
    data = _load_pyproject(project_root)

    names = [entry.lower() for entry in data["project"]["dependencies"]]
    assert any(name.startswith("flask") for name in names)


def test_dev_group_includes_pytest(project_root: Path) -> None:
    data = _load_pyproject(project_root)

    names = [entry.lower() for entry in data["dependency-groups"]["dev"]]
    assert any(name.startswith("pytest") for name in names)


def test_lockfile_exists_at_root(project_root: Path) -> None:
    assert (project_root / "uv.lock").is_file()


def test_tests_directory_and_conftest_exist(project_root: Path) -> None:
    assert (project_root / "tests").is_dir()
    assert (project_root / "tests" / "conftest.py").is_file()


def test_pytest_discovers_tests_from_project_root(project_root: Path) -> None:
    data = _load_pyproject(project_root)

    assert data["tool"]["pytest"]["ini_options"]["testpaths"] == ["tests"]


def test_running_interpreter_can_import_flask() -> None:
    import flask

    assert flask.Flask.__name__ == "Flask"
    assert importlib.metadata.version("flask").split(".")[0] == "3"


def test_python_runtime_meets_declared_minimum() -> None:
    assert sys.version_info >= (3, 11)

This file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit
``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every
Target inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose
on each build.

The application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per
declared access pattern::

    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)
    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)
    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status="open")

``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the
operations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver
for the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.

Values reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be
bound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated
against ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.
"""

from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence

"""Books persistence: the declared repository operations, read back through the public interface."""

from persistence import Database


def test_create_returns_stored_book_with_supplied_fields(db_session: Database) -> None:
    row = db_session.books.create(title="Dune", author="Frank Herbert")

    assert row.id is not None
    assert row.title == "Dune"
    assert row.author == "Frank Herbert"


def test_create_assigns_distinct_ids(db_session: Database) -> None:
    first = db_session.books.create(title="First", author="A")
    second = db_session.books.create(title="Second", author="A")

    assert first.id != second.id


def test_get_reads_back_created_book(db_session: Database) -> None:
    created = db_session.books.create(title="Emma", author="Jane Austen")

    fetched = db_session.books.get(id=created.id)

    assert fetched.id == created.id
    assert fetched.title == "Emma"
    assert fetched.author == "Jane Austen"


def test_get_returns_none_for_unknown_id(db_session: Database) -> None:
    created = db_session.books.create(title="Gone", author="A")
    db_session.books.delete(id=created.id)

    assert db_session.books.get(id=created.id) is None


def test_list_returns_books_in_order_added(db_session: Database) -> None:
    titles = ["ac-list-first", "ac-list-second", "ac-list-third"]
    created_ids = [db_session.books.create(title=t, author="ac-list-author").id for t in titles]

    listed_ids = [row.id for row in db_session.books.list()]

    mine = [i for i in listed_ids if i in created_ids]
    assert mine == created_ids


def test_delete_removes_book_from_next_list(db_session: Database) -> None:
    keep = db_session.books.create(title="ac-delete-keep", author="ac-delete-author")
    gone = db_session.books.create(title="ac-delete-gone", author="ac-delete-author")

    db_session.books.delete(id=gone.id)

    listed_ids = [row.id for row in db_session.books.list()]
    assert gone.id not in listed_ids
    assert keep.id in listed_ids


def test_created_book_is_visible_in_the_same_transaction(db_session: Database) -> None:
    before = {row.id for row in db_session.books.list()}

    created = db_session.books.create(title="Visible", author="A")

    after = {row.id for row in db_session.books.list()}
    assert after == before | {created.id}
